name.en: Fake NZTA text: “you have an unpaid road toll”

how.en: A text says you have an unpaid or overdue road toll and gives a link. The link goes to a site that looks like NZTA’s and asks for your card details to pay a small fee. Criminals then use the card to buy phones and gift cards. In one case sentenced in Auckland in June 2026, a 63-year-old lost $16,690.

text.en: A text claims to be from NZTA about an unpaid road toll.
It says the toll is overdue and you must pay now.
It links to a copy of the NZTA website.
The site takes your card details and criminals spend on your card.
NZTA: Your vehicle has an unpaid road toll of $4.20. Pay today to avoid a $65 penalty: [link]

en: A text about a toll with a link to pay.
A small amount with a bigger penalty if you don’t pay today.
A website asking for card details to pay a toll.
Don’t tap the link. Check tolls by typing the official NZTA address yourself.
If you entered card details, call your bank to block the card.
